bash check port without external commands
ctr pull and run alpine
text: ctr -n k8s.io image pull docker.io/library/alpine:latest; ctr -n k8s.io run --rm -t --net-host --mount type=bind,src=/root/,dst=/mnt/,options=rbind:rw docker.io/library/alpine:latest mypod ash

name: fish batch mv rename
git rebase all past commits preserving timestamps
text: git -c rebase.instructionFormat='%s%nexec GIT_COMMITTER_DATE="%cD" GIT_AUTHOR_DATE="%aD" git commit [-S] --amend --no-edit --reset-author' rebase [-i] [--root]

name: grep ignore blank or starting with #
kubectl curl pod
text: begin; set -lx pod debug-(date +%s); kubectl run --restart=Never --image=curlimages/curl $pod -- curl -fsSL {cursor} ; kubectl wait --for=create pod/$pod; kubectl logs --follow $pod; kubectl delete pod $pod; end

name: kubectl get all namespaced resources in ns
text: kubectl api-resources --verbs=list --namespaced -o name | xargs -n 1 kubectl get --show-kind --ignore-not-found -n {cursor}

name: kubectl go-template secret with embedded files
kubectl node-shell fzf interactive
text: kubectl node-shell (kubectl get nodes -o name | fzf)

name: kubectl replace pod
text: kubectl get pod -n {cursor} -o yaml | kubectl replace --force -f -

name: openssl check expiry of domain
text:
echo | openssl s_client -connect <domain>{cursor}:443 2> /dev/null | \
        awk '/-----BEGIN/,/END CERTIFICATE-----/' | \
        openssl x509 -noout -enddate

name: openstack server ips comma-delimited
text: openstack server list -c Name -c Networks | rg -o '[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}' | rg -v '^10\.' | sort | paste -s -d ',' -

name: openstack servers comma-delimited
text: openstack --os-project-name {cursor} server list -c Name -f value  | sort | paste -s -d ',' -
